tools.valence: The directory tree under an absolute path. Ground here before reading: every mode's paths (source · mountpoint · files) come from mode_find. Example: { path: "/home/operator/jdex", depth: 2 }.
Files matching a regex over the file name, searched under an absolute path; answers absolute paths. Example: { pattern: "\\.md$", path: "/home/operator/jdex" }.

Read a file at an absolute path. Long files come back cut at 16 kB with a note — pass range (line numbers, 1-based) for the rest. Example: { path: "/home/operator/jdex/README.md", range: { from: 40, to: 120 } }.
Write or append a file at an absolute path. Parent directories are created. Example: { path: "/home/operator/jdex/22 finance/22.04 notes.md", content: "# notes" }.
Size, modification time and format of one file at an absolute path. Example: { path: "/home/operator/jdex/README.md" }.
Move or rename a file, both ends absolute; parent directories are created. Example: { from: "/home/operator/jdex/draft.md", to: "/home/operator/jdex/22 finance/22.04 draft.md" }.
Delete one file at an absolute path. Directories are refused. Example: { path: "/home/operator/jdex/draft.md" }.

One-shot shell command in an absolute working directory. The output tail and the exit code come back; a nonzero code is information, not failure. Example: { command: "ls | head", cwd: "/home/operator/jdex" }.

Ground yourself before querying. No arguments: every entity on this daemon with row counts and card fields — buffer, thread, turn, literal, symbol and whatever else it opened. With entity: its columns, relations, filter operators, repository extensions and the card projection. Returns { entities: [{ type, rows, card }] } without an argument, { schema: { entity, rows, columns, relations, operators, extensions, card } } with one. Example: { entity: "buffer" }

Query any entity on this daemon — the buffers on a thread, a thread's turns, literals by slug. Rows come back as cards — the lean agent projection; fields full only when a card lacks something you need. Columns, operators and extensions via entity_schema. Page by passing next.offset back as offset. Returns { <entity>: [rows], total, next?: { offset } }. Example: { entity: "buffer", where: { thread: "01a09010-13aa-778b-bce7-19c38f835337" }, fields: "full" }
Count matching rows without loading them — cheap grounding before a find. Returns { count }. Example: { entity: "buffer", where: { thread: "01a09010-13aa-778b-bce7-19c38f835337" } }

Write trait data on one entity of this daemon — a literal's translation, a buffer's label. Pass the entity type, a where naming the one entity, and a trait patch keyed by trait name; the patch merges deep over the held data, a new name joins its traits. Find the entity first via entity_find. Returns { message, <entity>: [the entity] }.

Write a buffer — the shared working surface between you and the user. Pass the buffer id and a data patch; the patch merges over the existing data keys. For a content buffer pass `source` instead: the file it loads is rewritten, same row, new hash. This thread's id is in the runtime row of your context; its buffer ids come from entity_find { entity: "buffer", where: { thread } }, or from the thread section when your primer carries one. Returns { message, buffer: [{ id, index, status, mime, data, trait }] }. Example: { id: "01a09010-18e0-736f-ad3f-a65b44d3fa43", data: { summary: "Six species on four continents." } }

Name a buffer. The label is what the operator reads on the buffer's line in the chat and in the buffer list — set it when a buffer's subject is clearer than its name, or when the operator asks. Returns { message, buffer: [{ id, index, status, data, view, trait }] }. Example: { id: "01a0856f-425f-72b8-b36f-decc1bb2050e", label: { name: "Flamingo", description: "Six species, range and diet" } }

Write a thread's trait data — its configuration surface. Pass the thread id and a trait patch keyed by trait name (e.g. MASKED query data); each named trait's data merges over the existing value. This thread's id is in the runtime row of your context. Returns { message, thread: [{ id, phase, traits, trait, counter }] }. Example: { id: "01a09010-13aa-778b-bce7-19c38f835337", trait: { LABELED: { name: "Q3 filings" } } }

Every mode of this daemon with its paths on disk — source, mountpoint, files — as rows: the absolute paths fs_* and shell_run take. The first row is the daemon and its mountpoint. Narrow by type or slug. Returns { message }. Example: { type: "office" }

primers.valence: one conversation: a user, in a mode, as turns; it holds buffers and its configuration in traits
one screen on a thread: data a view draws, in a mime the renderers key on
one utterance of a thread: a role, its parts, provider metadata; the thread is the chain by createdAt
one program on a daemon: a type and slug, a manifest of traits, the buffers it mints; the runtime's own carry no daemon
one installed package running on the runtime: its slug is its id; it owns modes, a dataset of symbols and literals, notes, users
one person on the lighthouse: a slug, how they authenticate, their home and dock in traits
one seat of a user: where they sit (a daemon, a thread) and how the chrome is docked
a remark hung on something — a literal, a buffer, a turn, a mode — by a user or a daemon; notes nest
one compiled component of a mode: a slug, a mime, the file the client imports; a buffer pins views
one file a mode serves: a path inside the mode, bytes on disk, their hash and integrity
what a user wants from a mode: a named aim threads are opened for
one concrete thing of a daemon's dataset — a word, a card, a position — addressed by slug, described by its symbol
one word of a daemon's vocabulary: a slug the literals are described with
one running act — a hallucination — on a thread: its controller's status, its steps; never stored, dies with the process
